content:
jon: quick heads-up — Mark's reseller wants to run a weekend batch ramp on 3/28-3/29 across us-west1, eu-west1, and ap-northeast1. they said ~120k GPU hours over 48h. can the fleet support a sudden market-driven spike?
mark_partner: yup thats correct. it's a mix of embeddings backfill + nightly fine-tune jobs from 4 partners. they want a predictable SLA for the window and are asking about reserved capacity options and a fallback if we hit limits.
maya: 120k GPU hours over 48h = avg 2500 GPUs concurrently if they're running 24h. need to know concurrency shape — is it steady or spikey?
mark_partner: pattern is spikey. peak windows of ~6 hours each day with big bursts overnight. overall 2 big waves, each ~18 hours of sustained high throughput and short 30-60m peaks within them.
felipe: ops note: continuous batching will help, but KV cache & mem pressure could be material for long gpt-4-sized sequences. eu-west1 also has limited reserved pool this week.
rachel: cost angle — at list prices this weekend is ~ $X. We should propose a blended reserved+spot contract. partner expects a discount if we guarantee a min capacity.
ken: networking: partners will stream model checkpoints and embeddings out to S3. egress to partner bucket in eu-west1 will hit our peering limits if we parallelize too hard. need staged upload and per-region throttles.
jon: actionable ask: maya/felipe can you model a plan with (A) reserved capacity commit for critical baseline, (B) spot/ephemeral burst for peak, (C) canary strategy + automated rollback? also include cost delta and a recommended throttle policy.
maya: initial quick calc: reserve 900 GPUs in eu-west1 + 800 in us-west1 + 400 in ap-northeast1 for baseline — that's ~42k GPU hours over 48h (baseline). remaining ~78k -> burst/spot. i'll run a more precise hourly sim and upload numbers.
felipe: will add failure modes: node OOM during long sequences, nvlink pressure on multi-GPU pods, and scheduler backpressure. recommend circuit-breaker on per-partner queue at 80% of node allocation.
mark_partner: partner wants 99% job completion during the window. would they accept a staged SLA: 99% for reserved, 92% for burst?
rachel: staged SLA makes sense commercialy. we can offer credits for missed reserved SLA but not for spot. we should also add a penalty cap. I'll draft terms. :memo:
ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance window detected in eu-west1 3/27 22:00-23:30 — may reduce available capacity by ~120 GPUs.
felipe: ops-bot FYI that maintenance overlaps the pre-ramp health check. we should reschedule the maintenance or move pre-ramp to avoid it.
ken: suggestion: move heavy uploads to pre-stage via partner's cross-region replication in small chunks over 24h to avoid peering burst. provide an upload token with rate-limit.
maya: updated ask from the partner: they'd like a pre-provisioned canary of 50 GPUs per region 12h before the weekend start to validate configs and egress. fine with that.
jon: ok that helps. maya — add canary timeline + validation checklist. felipe — can you write the circuit-breaker config? something like: 
```
# example throttle pseudocode
if region_util > 0.8:\n  max_enqueue_rate = baseline_rate * 0.6\n  throttle_partner(queue, max_enqueue_rate)\nelse:\n  resume_normal()
```
felipe: will draft exact k8s HPAs and queue-shaper rules. also add automatic fallback to smaller model variant (quantized) if latency or OOM spikes.
rachel: on pricing: propose a blended rate: reserved @ 70% list + burst @ spot market + partner credit for egress. will show 3 scenarios (pessimistic, mid, optimistic).
mark_partner: partner agrees to the canary + staged SLA, but requests a test run next weekend (smaller scale) to validate network and billing. can we do a dry-run of ~10k GPU hours?
maya: yes we can schedule a dry-run. i'll run capacity sim for the dry-run and full run, include failure prob and expected throughput.
ken: FYI ap-northeast1 has a provider-side egress throttle window on Sunday midnight — we should avoid heavy uploads in that hour.
jon: next steps: (1) maya/felipe model + checklist by EOD tomorrow, (2) rachel draft commercial terms + pricing scenarios, (3) ken propose upload rate-limits and peering-safe pattern, (4) schedule ops review and dry-run next weekend. mark_partner will confirm partner side.
mark_partner: thanks all — will confirm the partner and aim for dry-run approval today. :thumbsup:
felipe: I'll add health probes and a post-run SLO report template (latency, completion rate, GPU-hours consumed, OOMs).
ops-bot: Note: created ticket INF-4521 for the weekend ramp plan and assigned to @maya, @felipe, @ken, @rachel.
jon: great — keep comms in this thread. +1 on the ticket. :eyes:
